label: Early copy step (output orig 1) in long sequences with e among the next original tokens
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase and almost entirely on the first two copy steps: recall_idx=1 (input = first original token, right after the step following <DEL>) holds about 80% of activation mass, and recall_idx=2 about 20%. Nothing in the original or delimiter phase, and nothing at recall_idx 0 or >=4. Rate goes up with sequence length (L=9 holds 57% of mass, L<=5 almost none). Within those positions it is sparse (2% of recall_idx=1 steps) and depends on content: activation is much stronger when the letter e appears among the next original tokens to be output (out_tok/next_out = e has about 15x lift; the top examples all have e at original positions 1-3), and when the first token is one of n, w, c, e, i, v, o, x. Top activations reach 3.5 on sequences like e e e r ... and c e e b .... It does not fire on first occurrences of a token. Predicate gets dev F1 about 0.30 and mass recall about 0.54. Adding the first-token set raises precision to about 0.55 but lowers recall. The position part is clean, but the content conditioning is only partly captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig3=e (+4.58), orig2=e (+4.41), orig4=e (+4.04), recall_idx=1 (+3.95), prev_tok=<DEL> (+3.95), orig1=e (+3.31). Lower it: in_tok=b (-4.33), in_first=1 (-4.24), orig1=p (-4.11), next_out=i (-2.99).
